decisions.reason: Selecting champagne-gold placement on the É accent does not change its required peak alignment with the Hero V.
The color-distribution decision applies a finish to the Hero V right arm without changing its approved geometry or construction rules.
The independent Satin Reflection finish selection is already fully captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the distribution decision requires no addition or edit.
Applying champagne gold to the second V right arm does not alter its optical construction, shared design DNA, or right-arm reach.
Keeping the remaining elements black does not change the E and L geometry, scale, or architectural-letterform requirements.
The selected gold highlight reinforces the perceived hierarchy but does not change the second V's required height relationships.
Applying champagne gold to the É accent does not change its required literal derivation from the Hero V terminal.
The distribution comparison was resolved, and the separate same-message request for kerning studies is already fully captured by the candidate's MODIFY.
The gold-distribution selection does not determine final kerning; the message's separate observation that spacing remains grouped is already represented as a runtime failure.
Using the existing exact geometry for material and kerning studies is consistent with, but does not modify, the established locked-asset preservation policy.
The selective champagne-gold distribution does not alter the approved shared baseline.
The material-distribution selection does not change the all-caps wordmark treatment.
